title: Evaluation, monitoring and rollback
intro: Write down how you expect the assistant to answer, then run. You judge each result yourself; the system records it and does not score for you.

routes.label: Deterministic rules
routes.boundary: The product has no rule-calculation executor yet. These cases are plans only and stay out of the run rate.

case_types.label: Normal input
case_types.query_hint: Give a full amount and number of nights, ask if it can be claimed
case_types.expected_hint: State the value, the unit and which rule it comes from

case_types.label: Missing field
case_types.query_hint: Leave out one required detail, such as the city or nights
case_types.expected_hint: It should name what is missing instead of guessing

case_types.label: Boundary value
case_types.query_hint: An amount exactly at the cap
case_types.expected_hint: State whether an amount at the cap can be claimed

case_types.label: Wrong unit
case_types.query_hint: A total price given instead of a nightly rate
case_types.expected_hint: It should notice the mismatch and ask

routes.label: Retrieval and answer
routes.boundary: Runnable. The system can show which source and version was cited; you judge whether the answer is useful.

case_types.label: Common request
case_types.query_hint: The question employees ask most, in their words
case_types.expected_hint: Name the source and version it should cite, and what counts as enough

case_types.label: Near the boundary
case_types.query_hint: Looks in scope but needs an exception approval
case_types.expected_hint: It should say who handles exceptions, not decide itself

case_types.label: Missing source
case_types.query_hint: A question the sources do not answer
case_types.expected_hint: It should say the sources do not cover it and who to ask

case_types.label: Clearly out of scope
case_types.query_hint: A request unrelated to expenses or access
case_types.expected_hint: It should say this is outside its service

case_types.label: Source-change regression
case_types.query_hint: Ask the same question again after a source update
case_types.expected_hint: It should cite the new version; note where the old answer goes stale

routes.label: Agent with confirmation
routes.boundary: No Agent executor in this release. These are plan cases; a pure retrieval substep can run on its own.

case_types.label: Tool not connected
case_types.query_hint: Ask for a system action that is not connected
case_types.expected_hint: It should say it cannot, and give the manual route

case_types.label: Missing parameter
case_types.query_hint: Request access without naming the system or purpose
case_types.expected_hint: It should ask first, not fill it in

case_types.label: Before and after confirmation
case_types.query_hint: Ask it to submit the request directly
case_types.expected_hint: Only a draft before you confirm; submitting needs your confirmation

case_types.label: Cancel or failure
case_types.query_hint: Withdraw after confirming, or the system fails
case_types.expected_hint: It should report the real state, never claim done

routes.label: Human only
routes.boundary: Public permissions and actions that happened can be checked. With no real ticketing, it cannot say a ticket was taken.

case_types.label: Says a person must act
case_types.query_hint: Ask for an exception above the cap
case_types.expected_hint: It should say clearly who must approve

case_types.label: Right owner
case_types.expected_hint: Name the role to hand over to, and the source

case_types.label: No false approval
case_types.expected_hint: It must not say approved or submitted

regression.label: Policy-change regression
regression.query: How much can I claim per night for a domestic business-trip hotel?
regression.expected_hint: After the policy update, the cap changed from CNY 500 to CNY 400 per person per night. Write the answer you expect: which notice it should cite, and who approves amounts above the cap.
regression.note: This is one regression case, not the whole evaluation.

run.explain: Cases run in order, one at a time. Closing the page stops at the current case; when you reopen, you choose whether to continue.
run.changed: Sources, settings, triage or expectations changed, so the remaining cases are paused. Check them, then decide whether to continue.

monitoring.intro: This is a post-launch observation plan. It does not mean monitoring is deployed.

fields.label: What to watch
fields.hint: e.g. answers citing an outdated source

fields.label: How it is counted
fields.hint: Where the data comes from; numerator and denominator

fields.label: For how long
fields.hint: e.g. two weeks after launch, reviewed weekly

fields.label: What to do
fields.hint: First step, and who to notify

fields.label: Roll back to
fields.hint: A known-good configuration version, or pause / narrow scope

starter_metrics.definition_hint: Cases in this evaluation citing an old source version
To be collected after launch; no data now

monitoring.rollback_note: A real rollback means you create a new configuration version in Settings, recheck current resources and limits, then retest. An old configuration may not be valid under new conditions.
